cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1-3), is the one telling this. In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel come to inquire of the LORD and sit down before him. The word of the LORD comes, and God's message for the elders opens with a question: "Have you come to inquire of Me?"

cards.question: The elders of Israel came to Ezekiel to inquire of the LORD. What is the Lord GOD's answer to them?

answers.text: He will not be consulted by them
He will answer them in a dream

cards.text: Then God tells Ezekiel to confront them with the abominations of their fathers. He starts at the beginning: on the day He chose Israel, He made Himself known to them in the land of Egypt and said, "I am the LORD your God."

cards.question: On that same day in Egypt, God swears an oath to Israel. What does He swear to do?

answers.text: Bring them out into a land He picked for them
Give them the best land in all of Egypt
Make them the rulers over all of Egypt

cards.question: While they're still in Egypt, God tells each of them to throw away the abominations before his eyes. What else must they not defile themselves with?

cards.text: But they rebel against Him and refuse to listen.

cards.question: Israel rebels and refuses to listen. True or false: none of them cast away the abominations before their eyes.

cards.text: They don't forsake the idols of Egypt either. That's the whole office getting the new policy email, and the next morning NOBODY has changed a single thing.
So God resolves to pour out His wrath on them right there in the land of Egypt. But He acts for the sake of His name.

cards.question: God acts for the sake of His name, so it won't be profaned in someone's eyes. Whose eyes?

answers.text: The nations they were living among
The elders of their own tribes

cards.text: So God brings them out of Egypt and leads them into the wilderness. Me? I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and the farthest I ever moved was when somebody dug around for the tape.
In the wilderness, God gives them His statutes and ordinances. He says the man who does these things will live by them.

cards.question: God also gives Israel His Sabbaths as a sign between Him and them. What is that sign for?

answers.text: So they'd know He's the LORD who makes them holy
So they'd know when to plant and when to harvest
So their enemies would be afraid of them

cards.question: God gave Israel His statutes and His Sabbaths. True or false: out in the wilderness, Israel follows His statutes and keeps His Sabbaths holy.

cards.text: They reject His ordinances and utterly profane His Sabbaths, so God resolves to put an end to them in the wilderness. And AGAIN, He acts for the sake of His name, so it won't be profaned in the eyes of the nations who watched Him bring them out.

cards.question: With an uplifted hand, God swears to that generation in the wilderness that He will not bring them into the ___ He had given them.
God gives the reason for His oath: they kept rejecting His ordinances and profaning His Sabbaths, for their ___ continually went after their idols.
The generation God brought out of Egypt keeps rebelling against Him in the wilderness. True or false: God destroys that generation and brings them to an end in the wilderness.

cards.text: Instead, God looks on them with pity and does not destroy them. Friend, ONE batch burns and I'm ready to haul the whole oven out to the curb.
Now God turns to their children, out in the wilderness. He tells them not to walk in the statutes of their fathers or defile themselves with their fathers' idols.

cards.question: God tells the children not to walk in their fathers' statutes. Whose statutes does He tell them to walk in instead?
God also tells the children to keep His Sabbaths holy. True or false: the children walk in His statutes and carefully keep His ordinances.

cards.text: The children rebel and profane His Sabbaths too. That's the brand-new planner you buy in January that's blank by February.
God resolves to pour out His wrath on them in the wilderness. But once again, He withholds His hand for the sake of His name.

cards.question: Because the children keep rejecting His statutes and fixing their eyes on their fathers' idols, God swears an oath to them in the wilderness with an uplifted hand. What does He swear?

answers.text: He'll scatter them among the nations
He'll make them a great empire
He'll send them back to Egypt

cards.text: Then comes a hard part. God says He gave them over to statutes that were not good, and pronounced them unclean through their gifts: the sacrifice of every firstborn in the fire.
Then God tells Ezekiel to tell the house of Israel another way their fathers blasphemed Him, once He'd brought them into the land He swore to give them.

cards.question: In the land God swore to give them, where do the fathers go to offer their sacrifices?

answers.text: On any high hill or under any leafy tree
Only at the altar God chose for them
In the courts of the LORD's house

cards.question: In the land, the fathers offer their sacrifices on any high hill or under any leafy tree. God says those offerings ___ Him.
God asks them, "What is this high place to which you go?" When this was written, what was that place still called?
Now God asks the house of Israel in Ezekiel's day if they'll defile themselves the way their fathers did. True or false: He says they're still doing it, right up to this day.

cards.text: So God gives the same answer He gave at the start: as surely as He lives, He will not be consulted by them. They came in with ONE question and got the whole family history.
Then God takes on something the house of Israel says: "Let us be like the nations, like the peoples of the lands…"

cards.question: The house of Israel wants to be like the nations. What do they say they'd be serving?
They want to be like the nations, serving wood and stone. True or false: God says what they have in mind will come to pass.

cards.text: As surely as He lives, God says He will rule over them with a strong hand, an outstretched arm and outpoured wrath.

cards.question: With that same strong hand, God will bring them out from the peoples and ___ them from the lands where they've been scattered.

cards.text: Then God will bring them into the wilderness of the nations.

cards.question: What will God do with His people there in the wilderness of the nations?

answers.text: Enter into judgment face to face
Lead them by a pillar of fire

cards.text: It's just like He judged their fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt. He'll make them pass under the rod and bring them into the bond of the covenant.

cards.question: God will purge out the ones who rebel and transgress against Him. True or false: those rebels will still enter the land of Israel.

cards.text: Then God says something you might not see coming. He tells the house of Israel, "Go and serve your idols, every one of you."

cards.question: God tells the house of Israel to go serve their idols. But what does He say will happen afterward?

answers.text: They will surely listen to Him
They will forget Him for good
They will go back to Egypt

cards.text: And when they listen, they'll no longer defile His holy name with their gifts and idols.

cards.question: God says the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Him in the land. Where?
Earlier, God refused to be consulted by them. True or false: on His holy mountain, God says He will accept them.

cards.text: There, God says He will require their offerings and choice gifts, along with all their holy sacrifices.

cards.question: When God gathers them from the lands where they were scattered, He says He will accept them as a pleasing ___.

cards.text: God will show His holiness through them in the sight of the nations. Then they will know He is the LORD, when He brings them into the land He swore to give their fathers.

cards.question: Back in the land, they'll remember their ways and all the deeds that defiled them. How does God say they'll feel about themselves?

answers.text: They will be proud of themselves

cards.question: They will know He is the LORD when He deals with them for the sake of His name, and not according to their ___ ways.

cards.text: After round after round of rebellion, God says He will deal with them for the sake of His name, not their record. And as a stamper who got pulled out of the back of a junk drawer, friend, I know a little something about that.
